diagnostic_evidence.quote: can be continuously extended to a continuous mapping $\gamma_{1}:H^{1}\left(  \omega,\Delta\right)  \rightarrow H^{-1/2}\left(  \Gamma\right)$

issues.failure_explanation: The definition is ill-posed as written: the normal trace gamma_1 is only defined on H^1(omega,Delta) (as stated immediately before), so the set-builder condition 'gamma_1 v in H^{-1/2}(Gamma)' is meaningless for v in H^1(omega) minus H^1(omega,Delta); and the declared 'natural norm' requires gamma_1 v in L^2(Gamma), which does not follow even for v in H^1(omega,Delta), where the trace lies only in H^{-1/2}(Gamma). Thus H^1(omega,Gamma) is not a well-defined normed space.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define H^1(omega,Gamma) := H^1(omega,Delta) (equivalently {v in H^1(omega,Delta) : gamma_1 v in H^{-1/2}(Gamma)}) and equip it with the norm sqrt(||v||^2_{H^1(omega)} + ||gamma_1 v||^2_{H^{-1/2}(Gamma)}), or explicitly restrict to elements possessing an L^2(Gamma) normal trace.
issues.overall_effect: The space H^1(Omega,S_R) built on this definition is used in the statement and proof of thm:C_Friedrich; no theorem's truth is affected because the intended meaning is recoverable, but the object itself is formally undefined.
issues.title: Ill-defined space and norm H^1(omega,Gamma) in DefH1Gamma
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition repairs the object; every subsequent use (thm:C_Friedrich, CorTrace) survives with the intended reading, with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: H=\left\{  v\in H^{1}\left(  \Omega,S_{R}\right)  \mid\partial_{r} v-\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  z\right)  v=0\ \text{ on }S_{R}\text{ for some }z\in\mathbb{C}_{\geq0}\right\}
(The completeness of $H$ follows from the continuity of the $\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)  $ operator by \Cref{thm:DtN}.)

issues.failure_explanation: The contradiction argument asserts that the weak limit u lies in H = union over z in C_{>=0} of {v : partial_r v = DtN(z) v}. This union is not a closed subspace: no single z is fixed along the sequence (z_k may even be unbounded), so 'u in H', and hence the existence of s with DtN(s)u = partial_r u = 0 used together with thm:DtN.(iii), is unjustified; the claimed completeness of H does not follow from continuity of DtN. Moreover the sequence is assumed to satisfy ||partial_r v_k||_{L^2(S_R)} -> 0, which is stronger than the hypothesis ||partial_r v||_{H^{-1/2}(S_R)} -> 0, and partial_r v_k in L^2(S_R) is not guaranteed for v_k in H^1(Omega,S_R).

failure_location.quote: Since this sequence is bounded in $H$, it admits a weakly convergent subsequence with weak limit $u\in H$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bypass the weak limit: test the boundary condition against v_k and use thm:DtN.(iii) to get (n-2)/2 ||v_k||^2_{L^2(S_R)} <= |<DtN(s_k)v_k, v_k>| = |<partial_r v_k, v_k>| <= ||partial_r v_k||_{H^{-1/2}(S_R)} ||v_k||_{H^{1/2}(S_R)} -> 0, hence ||v_k||_{L^2(S_R)} -> 0; compactness of the H^1(Omega) embedding then gives v_k -> c constant in L^2(Omega) and on S_R with ||c||_{L^2(Omega)} = 1, so c vanishes on S_R and thus c = 0, a contradiction.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the Friedrichs inequality (thm:C_Friedrich) is incomplete as written, and CorTrace, whose proof invokes thm:C_Friedrich, inherits the gap. The statement of thm:C_Friedrich itself is true and the s-independent constant survives.
issues.title: Unjustified weak-limit claim in the proof of the Friedrichs inequality
issues.why_classification: A short direct argument with existing ingredients (thm:DtN.(iii), compact trace embedding) closes the gap; the statement, the s-independent constant, and all consequences are preserved, so no new lemma or weakening is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The situation is different for $\mu=0$ where $M_{0}^{2}(k)$ admits no lower bound for $k\rightarrow0$ that is linear in $1/k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed bound does not follow for n = 2: via <DtN(s)g, g> = sum z_{m,nu}(s)|g_hat_{m,j}|^2 the (m,nu)=(0,0) mode contributes ∓Im z_{0,0}(s)|g_hat_{0,1}|^2 with ∓Im z_{0,0}(s) <= c_2 + |Im s| (thm:zmn.(iii)), which is not O(|Im s|): for s = i k, k -> 0^+, and g = Y_{0,1}, the contribution 2/(pi M_0^2(k)) ~ pi/(2 (log k)^2) is unbounded relative to |Im s| = k. The theorem's stated estimate with C(n)||g||^2_{H^{1/2},s} remains valid because (c_2 + |Im s|)||g||^2_{L^2} <= (c_2+1)||g||^2_{H^{1/2},s}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the intermediate bound by ∓Im<DtN(s)g, g> <= (c_2 + |Im s|)||g||^2_{L^2(S_1)} <= (c_2+1)||g||^2_{H^{1/2}(S_1),s}, which yields exactly the stated estimate.
issues.overall_effect: A proof step for part (iv) of thm:DtN is false for n=2 as written; the theorem's stated bound is correct and its use elsewhere (thm:C_Friedrich via part (iii)) is unaffected.
issues.title: False intermediate |Im s|-bound for n=2 in the proof of thm:DtN
issues.why_classification: One-line correction of the intermediate estimate; the stated theorem, its quantifiers, and its constant structure all survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The case-split estimates are miscalculated. With n = 2*nu+2 the radial integrals give F^2_{m,j} = (d^2-R^2)/2 for m+nu=0 (not log(d/R)) and F^2_{m,j} = R^{2nu+2}(1-(R/d)^{2(m+nu)-2})/(2(m+nu-1)) for m+nu>=2 (not R^{2nu}/(2(m+nu))); e.g. nu=1/2, m=1, R=1, d=2 yields F^2 = 1/2 > 1/3 as claimed. The G^2 bounds (powers R^{2nu+2}, denominators m+nu-2) are likewise too small, and H^2_{m,j} uses m^2 where the Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalue lambda_m = m(m+n-2) belongs, underestimating the H^1 seminorm for n>=3. Consequently the uniform bound max{F^2,G^2,H^2} <= (d/R)^4 R^{2nu}(1+R^2)(m+2nu)(nu+2) fails for m=nu=0, where its right side vanishes but F^2_{0,0} = (d^2-R^2)/2 > 0, so the displayed quantity is also not the true H^1 norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the integrals: F^2_{m,j} = (d^2-R^2)/2 for m=nu=0, R^{2nu+2} log(d/R) for m+nu=1, and R^{2nu+2}(1-(R/d)^{2(m+nu)-2})/(2(m+nu-1)) for m+nu>=2; G^2_{m,j} <= (m+2nu)^2 R^{2nu}/(2(m+nu)) for m+nu>=1 (and 0 for m=nu=0); replace m^2 by lambda_m = m(m+n-2); summability against ||g||^2_{H^{1/2}(S_R)} and hence the same continuity conclusion follow with adjusted constants.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of PropProblems.2a (continuity of the s=0 solution operator from H^{1/2}(S_R) to H^1_loc) is invalid as written; the well-posedness statement itself is correct and is all that the rest of the paper uses.
issues.title: Incorrect integral estimates in the s=0 continuity proof (PropProblems.2a)
issues.why_classification: Routine recomputation of elementary integrals repairs the proof; no new lemma, construction, or weakening is needed and the statement and all its uses survive.
